Q1.question_text: Explain data structures and their types.
Q1.student_answer:
A data structure is a specialized format for organizing, processing, retrieving and storing data in computer memory so it can be used efficiently. These are broadly split into linear and non-linear.

1. Linear Data Structure: Elements are arranged in a sequential, linear order where each element is connected to its previous and next neighbor. • Array: A fixed-size collection of elements of the same data type stored at contiguous memory locations. • Linked List: A sequence of nodes where each node contain data and a reference to the next node, allowing flexible memory allocation. • Stack: A collection that follows last in first out, i only one door for input & output. • Queue: A collection that follows first-in-first-out, image it as a pipe.

Non-Linear Data Structure: Elements are arranged severally; instead they connect in hierarchical or network relationship. • Tree: A hierarchical structure consisting of a root node with branching child node, commonly used for file system. • Graph: A network of nodes (vertices) connected by links (edges), used to represent web link social media connections or map.

criteria_breakdown.description: A data structure is a specialized way of organizing, storing, and managing data in computer memory so that it can be accessed, processed, and updated efficiently.
Classification into linear (elements arranged sequentially/adjacently) and non-linear data structures (hierarchical or network relationships).
Correctly identify examples of linear and non-linear data structures.

Q2.question_text: Explain an algorithm and the characteristics of a good algorithm.
Q2.student_answer:
An algorithm is a step by step procedure or set of rules designed to perform a specific task or solve a defined problem.

Characteristics of Good Algorithm: A high-quality algorithm must meet several key technical and practical standards.

Inputs: It must have zero or more well-defined inputs.

Outputs: It must produce at least one clearly defined output matching the goal.

Definiteness: Each step must be completely unambiguous and clearly stated.

Effectiveness: Every instruction must be basic enough to be carried out exactly.

Language Independence: The underlying logic must apply to any programming language.

Finiteness: It must terminate after a specific limited number of steps.

Feasibility: It must work effectively within available system resources like time and memory.

criteria_breakdown.description: An algorithm is a finite set of well-defined, step-by-step instructions designed to solve a problem or perform a computation.
List and describe key characteristics of a good algorithm.

Q3.question_text: Explain complexity analysis and its types.
Q3.student_answer:
Complexity analysis is a technique used to measure the efficiency of an algorithm in terms of computer resources it consumes as input size grows.

Types of complexity Analysis:

Time complexity: Measure the total execution time required by an algorithm to run to completion as a function of the input size.

Space complexity: Measures the total amount of working memory or storage space required by the algorithm during its lifecycle.

Cases Used in Complexity Analysis:

Worst case: The maximum possible resources required for any input of a given size, typically denoted using Big O notation.

Best case: The minimum possible resources required for most ideal input scenarios, typically denoted using Big omega (Ω).

Average case: The expected amount of resources required taken over all possible inputs, typically denoted using Big theta (Θ).

criteria_breakdown.description: Complexity analysis evaluates the efficiency of an algorithm with respect to input size by determining how time and memory requirements grow.
Time complexity measures the execution time or number of operations required by an algorithm relative to input size.
Space complexity measures the amount of memory or storage required by an algorithm during execution.
Mention of best, average, and worst case analysis for evaluating performance under different conditions.

Q4.student_answer:
An array is a linear data structure that stores elements of the same data types in contiguous memory location allowing direct access to any element using an index.

A linked list is a linear data structure where elements are not stored in contiguous memory location but are instead linked memory locations together sequentially using pointers or references within each node.

Key Differences:

- Memory Allocation: Arrays use fixed, contiguous memory; linked lists use dynamic scattered memory.
- Access speed: Arrays allow instant access via index. Linked require traversing from the start node.
- Insertion / Deletion: Arrays require shifting elements; linked list required updating only a few pointers.

criteria_breakdown.description: An array is a linear data structure storing elements of the same data type in contiguous memory locations with fixed size and fast index-based access.
A linked list is a linear data structure of nodes storing data and pointers/references to the next node in non-contiguous memory, supporting dynamic sizing and efficient insertion/deletion.
